input.rationale: Compliant: no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right runs against Sparkling anywhere in the Agreement, and Garman has no right of access to Sparkling systems. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "verify", "records", "premises", "monitor", "report" and "certif" return nothing operative. Addressing the two residual points: (1) § 14 read in full (p0094-p0101) is a purely mutual definitional clause - the phrase "accounting records for which access is obtained by the other party pursuant to this Agreement" is descriptive of the scope of Confidential Information and is conditioned on access obtained under some other provision; § 14 contains only the definition and the six standard carve-outs (a)-(f), with no entry, examination, delivery or access mechanism, and § 1(b) simply cross-refers the definition to § 14. (2) The Schedules are incorporated by p0019 ("The following is a summary of the Schedules, which shall form an integral part of this Agreement") but appear in the text only as titles - Fee Schedule; Software and Documentation; Authorized Locations and Software copies; Specifications, Modifications, Data Conversion; Implementation and Training; Telephone Support - none of which is a reporting, certification or verification schedule, and no operative clause (including § 11, which is a bare obligation to pay the Fee Schedule fees) imports any usage-reporting or true-up right from them. § 3 imposes substantive use limits only; § 20 is time-of-the-essence and notices boilerplate; § 17(b) is a one-off post-termination self-certification of destruction/return with no vendor entry, auditor or system access. Because no audit right binds us, the AUDIT parameters (frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access) cannot arise, and the absence of any such right is at least as favorable as the playbook preferred position. Inserting frequency/notice/cost machinery would create a new Customer obligation and enlarge Garman's rights, so the correct minimal action is no edit.
